title: Capacity hold, hiring-flare & price-sensitivity playbook
summary: Playbook for short-window capacity holds (30/90/180d), a prioritized headcount salvage ladder (FTE vs contractor vs freeze), and a simple per-token pricing sensitivity matrix to trigger hiring/price actions.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook for Finance + Ops to execute a short-notice capacity shortage or price-compression event. Focus is on: (1) preserve 30d critical runway, (2) a 90d reorg/hiring ladder to avoid SLA breaches, (3) a 180d recovery plan with pricing levers. Intended audience: CFO, Head of Ops, Eng Leads, Revenue Ops.

TL;DR:
- Critical buffer: hold 12–14% of committed GPU capacity as emergency reserve for 30 days.
- Hiring ladder: delay non-customer-facing hires first, freeze or convert near-term IC hires to contractors, preserve 60% of SRE/serving-runtime hires.
- Pricing lever: implement a 3-band cadence: +10% (soft), +20% (moderate), +35% (hard) per-token corridor depending on utilization spike and gross margin erosion.

Assumptions (model inputs):
- Monthly hosted revenue run-rate: $6.2M
- Gross margin baseline (hosted): 62%
- Token unit cost (avg): $0.0009/token (weighted mix)
- Committed Dedicated & Private fixed costs: $2.1M/mo (amortized)
- Average lead-time to recruit senior infra engineer: 10–12 weeks
- Contractor cost uplift: 1.8x of FTE run-rate for short bursts

30 / 90 / 180-day scenarios (high level):
- Scenario A (Mild demand shock, -15% revenue, one-time):
  * 30d: use burst credits, hold 10% capacity, defer non-core hires, expected runway delta +18 days.
  * 90d: convert 2 mid-level open roles to contractors, renegotiate 2 cloud reservations, estimated saving $220k/quarter.
  * 180d: reprice non-committed slab customers (soft +10%).
- Scenario B (Sustained demand drop, -35% revenue for 3 months):
  * 30d: activate capacity-hold at 14%, cancel discretionary spend, target runway +45 days.
  * 90d: hiring freeze for product/growth hires, 30% of infra hires delayed 8–12 weeks, contractors for critical infra sprints. Estimated quarterly save: $1.1M.
  * 180d: tiered pricing +20% on new signups and renegotiate enterprise discounts.
- Scenario C (Price compression + higher unit cost due to spot market):
  * 30d: enable conservative quantization rollout on 2 high-cost models, drop heavy-emedding frequency cache TTLs, short-term unit cost down 8–12%.
  * 90d: accelerate Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization and autoscaling, re-evaluate slab terms with top 5 customers.
  * 180d: hard pricing +35% corridor if unit economics cannot be recovered otherwise.

Headcount mitigation ladder (prioritized order, timeline in weeks):
- Tier 0 (do not touch): critical SRE oncall staffing, serving-runtime team product owners on active incidents (preserve 100% coverage).
- Tier 1 (delay without immediate product risk; 2–6w): non-customer-facing research hires, intern/onboardings, vendor training subscriptions.
- Tier 2 (convert or contractor; 6–12w): mid-level infra, platform engineers on long backlog items -> convert to 6–12w contractor engagements.
- Tier 3 (defer/ditch; 12–24w): new feature hires for greenfield product experimentation, some growth marketing roles.
- Contractor budget carve-out example (quarter view):
  * 2x senior infra contractors (12w) @ $40k/week total -> $480k quarter
  * Equivalent FTE run-rate for 2 hires (fully burdened): $260k quarter -> delta $220k (we accept uplift to avoid recruitment time).

Pricing sensitivity matrix (simple):
- Inputs: elasticity per cohort (enterprise: -0.15, mid-market: -0.35, PLG/free-to-paid cohort: -0.9).
- Model output (illustrative):
  * +10% price -> revenue change: enterprise +1.5% (accounts churn low), mid-market -3.5%, PLG -9% -> net revenue roughly flat in small events.
  * +20% price -> enterprise -3%, mid-market -9%, PLG -18% -> net revenue -6% (but margin improves).
  * +35% price -> enterprise -8%, mid-market -18%, PLG -30% -> net revenue -14% but unit economics recover strongly.
- Trigger rules (proposed):
  * Soft band (+10%): trigger when 4-week rolling unit-cost gap > 6% and margin erosion projected in next 60d.
  * Moderate (+20%): when gap > 12% or runway reduction < 45d.
  * Hard (+35%): when gap > 20% and capacity reductions cannot recover margin within 90d.

Simple numeric sensitivity table (quarterly view — illustrative):
- Base (no price change): revenue $18.6M, gross margin 62%, gross profit $11.5M.
- +10%: revenue $18.4M (churned cohorts), gross margin 68%, gross profit $12.5M.
- +20%: revenue $17.4M, gross margin 72%, gross profit $12.5M.
- +35%: revenue $16.0M, gross margin 78%, gross profit $12.5M.
Note: gross profit numbers flatten because price increases disproportionately hit high-elasticity PLG usage. This is acceptable when protecting margin but must be balanced with long-term adoption metrics.

Short checklist for Ops + Finance activation (playbook steps):
1) Finance runs quick sim (one-pager) with updated MTD usage and unit-costs (owner: Priya) — 48h.
2) Ops calculates capacity hold percentage and marks burst-credit pool (owner: Liam) — 24h.
3) Product & Sales: identify top 20 customers at risk of reprice churn (owner: Aisha) — 72h.
4) People Ops: freeze/convert hires as per ladder and approve contractors (owner: Marco) — 96h.
5) Executive: approve temporary pricing band and communication strategy (owner: Tess) — 1 week.

Risks & mitigations:
- Customer churn from abrupt pricing -> mitigation: two-week pilot + grandfathering for existing enterprise deals, targeted credits for PLG cohorts.
- Slower feature velocity -> mitigation: prioritize security/ops work and accept short-term backlog growth.
- Contractor dependency -> mitigation: limit contractor horizon to 12 weeks and require knowledge-transfer milestones.

Quick model snippets (for spreadsheet handoff):
- Inputs: current tokens/mo, customer cohort distribution by % revenue, unit-cost by model family, committed fixed monthly amortization.
- Outputs: projected revenue, gross margin, runway days, hiring delta (FTE vs contractor), "price-triggers" flags.
Example rows (paste into sheet):
Cohort, Revenue%, Tokens/mo, Elasticity
Enterprise, 58, 1,200,000, -0.15
Mid-market, 27, 600,000, -0.35
PLG, 15, 2,200,000, -0.9

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Exec decision: acceptable maximum PLG churn for hard price lane? (quant threshold)
- People Ops: pre-approved contractor cap $/quarter?
- Sales: grace / grandfather rules for enterprise discount windows?

Immediate next steps (owners & due dates):
- Hand off the numeric workbook template to Ops (Liam) — due 2026-11-20.
- Finance to run 3 sensitivity runs (mild/moderate/severe) with live MTD usage (Priya) — due 2026-11-22.
- People Ops to produce a list of at-risk open reqs and contractor bench (Marco) — due 2026-11-24.

Notes to self / rough thoughts: 
- We may want a small A/B test for +10% on new PLG signups only for 7 days to measure elasticity more precisely before ramping.
- Consider an emergency comms template for enterprise + mid-market so Sales can proactively offer limited grandfathering/credits.
- Flag: quantization rollouts can be a near-term win vs pricing for certain heavy models — coordinate with Applied ML.

Appendix (rough math snippets, keep in sheet):
- Unit cost reduction from quantization on model X = 18% (assumed after infra changes).
- Contractor to FTE uplift and FTE fully-burdened numbers included in template tab 'hc-bridge'.
